memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. When he saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed down with his face to the ground. - Gen 19:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two angels arrive at Sodom - the same messengers who had just eaten at Abraham's table. But notice where they find Lot: "sitting in the gateway of the city." In the ancient world, the city gate was the place of leadership and influence. Lot, who once merely pitched his tents near Sodom, is now seated in its gate, a settled leader of a doomed city. The drift that began with a glance has become a whole way of life.

Yet even here, mercy comes looking for him. Judgement is about to fall, but before it does, God sends messengers to rescue Lot. In the midst of a wicked city, God had not forgotten the one man who still, in some faltering way, belonged to Him.

This is the tender persistence of God's grace. Lot had made poor choices for years, compromising steadily, embedding himself in a place he never should have called home. And still God pursued him with rescue. Grace goes looking for the compromised believer.

Peter later calls Lot "righteous," a man "distressed by the depraved conduct" around him (2 Pet 2:7) - a true believer, though a deeply compromised one. If you have drifted, if you're settled somewhere you know you shouldn't be, take heart: God's mercy still comes looking. The same Jesus who "came to seek and to save the lost" (Luke 19:10) pursues His own even into the places their choices have led them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you drifted into a place you never intended to settle?
- Can you trust that God's mercy still comes looking for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your mercy comes looking even for the compromised and the drifting. Where I have settled somewhere I shouldn't be, pursue me, rescue me, and draw me back to You.
Amen.
